nodes.title: The betweenness group of the rationals is closed and highly homogeneous

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered set, and say that $b$ lies strictly between $a$ and $c$ when $a < b < c$ or $c < b < a$. The betweenness automorphism group of $\alpha$ is the subgroup of the group of permutations of $\alpha$ consisting of the permutations $\sigma$ such that, for all $a, b, c \in \alpha$, $b$ lies strictly between $a$ and $c$ if and only if $\sigma(b)$ lies strictly between $\sigma(a)$ and…
nodes.title: The betweenness automorphism group of a linear order

nodes.summary: Let $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb{Q})$ be the group of all permutations of the set $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb{Q})$ is closed in the topology of pointwise convergence on the permutations of $\mathbb{Q}$, and it is highly homogeneous: for every natural number $k$ it has a single orbit on the $k$-element subsets of $\mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.title: The symmetric group of the rationals is closed and highly homogeneous

nodes.title: The automorphism group of a countably infinite dense circular order is closed and highly homogeneous

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a circularly ordered set with non-strict circular betweenness relation $\operatorname{btw}$. The automorphism group of $\alpha$ is the subgroup of the group of permutations of $\alpha$ consisting of the permutations $\sigma$ such that, for all $a, b, c \in \alpha$, $\operatorname{btw}(a, b, c)$ holds if and only if $\operatorname{btw}(\sigma(a), \sigma(b), \sigma(c))$ holds.
nodes.title: The automorphism group of a circular order

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a circular order, and write $\operatorname{sbtw}(x, y, z)$ for its strict betweenness relation ($y$ lies strictly between $x$ and $z$ going around the circle). For $a, b, c, d \in \alpha$, the pairs $a, b$ and $c, d$ separate each other when either $\operatorname{sbtw}(a, c, b)$ and $\operatorname{sbtw}(b, d, a)$ both hold, or $\operatorname{sbtw}(a, d, b)$ and $\operatorname{sbtw}(b, c, a)$ both…
nodes.title: Separation of pairs in a circular order

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $<$ and let $a, b, c \in \alpha$. Then $b$ lies strictly between $a$ and $c$ when either $a < b$ and $b < c$, or $c < b$ and $b < a$.
nodes.title: Strict betweenness

nodes.summary: For every set $\alpha$, the group of all permutations of $\alpha$ is highly homogeneous: for every natural number $k$, any $k$-element subset of $\alpha$ can be carried to any other $k$-element subset of $\alpha$ by some permutation of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: The full symmetric group is highly homogeneous

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group of permutations of a set $\alpha$. Then $G$ is highly homogeneous when, for every natural number $k$, it acts transitively on the $k$-element subsets of $\alpha$: for any two $k$-element subsets $X$ and $Y$ of $\alpha$ there is some $g \in G$ with $g(X) = Y$.
nodes.title: Highly homogeneous permutation groups

nodes.summary: The group of order automorphisms of $\mathbb{Q}$, that is, of the permutations $\sigma$ of $\mathbb{Q}$ such that $a < b$ if and only if $\sigma(a) < \sigma(b)$ for all $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}$, is closed in the topology of pointwise convergence on the permutations of $\mathbb{Q}$, where $\mathbb{Q}$ carries the discrete topology, and it is highly homogeneous: for every natural number $k$ it has a single orbit on the…
nodes.title: The order-automorphism group of the rationals is closed and highly homogeneous

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ equipped with a relation $<$, the order automorphism group of $\alpha$ is the subgroup of the group of permutations of $\alpha$ consisting of the permutations $\sigma$ such that for all $a, b \in \alpha$, $a < b$ holds if and only if $\sigma(a) < \sigma(b)$ holds.
nodes.title: Order automorphism group

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$, the pointwise convergence topology on the group of permutations of $\alpha$ is the topology induced by the map sending a permutation $\sigma$ to the underlying function $\sigma \colon \alpha \to \alpha$, where $\alpha$ carries the discrete topology and the space of functions $\alpha \to \alpha$ carries the product topology.
nodes.title: Pointwise convergence topology on permutations

nodes.title: The separation group of a countably infinite dense circular order is closed and highly homogeneous

nodes.summary: For a circular order $\alpha$, the separation-preserving group of $\alpha$ is the subgroup of the group of permutations of $\alpha$ consisting of the permutations $\sigma$ such that for all $a, b, c, d \in \alpha$, the pairs $a, b$ and $c, d$ separate each other if and only if the pairs $\sigma(a), \sigma(b)$ and $\sigma(c), \sigma(d)$ separate each other.
nodes.title: Separation-preserving permutation group

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
